# **Cal Hacks 13.0 — Assistive Glasses Team Plan**

Oct 23, 2026 · @Marvin

## **TL;DR**

We build one voice-first assistant on Meta Ray-Ban glasses that describes what is ahead, remembers what the user saw, and drives their browser. We demo one tight loop well instead of four shaky features.

**Pitch (draft):** Blind and low-vision adults rely on a cane and on other people for things a camera can now help with: reading a crossing signal, checking a packed order, sending an email, finding their keys. Our app streams frames from the glasses, listens through their mics and answers out loud. It remembers what it has seen, so "where did I leave my keys?" and "what was my brother wearing?" have answers. A live family dashboard lets someone they trust see alerts and step in.

**Tracks we target:** Meta (Bringing People Closer Together), Anthropic, Cartesia, Moss and SpacetimeDB, plus the general Best People-First, Best Hardware and Most Technically Complex prizes. Details are in Sponsor tracks below.

**Decisions to make tonight:**

* ☐ **Name the community.** Our four features fit blind and low-vision users; "cognitive disabilities" fits the memory and step-by-step task help. Anthropic judges on how narrowly we name it. Recommendation: blind and low-vision adults who work.  
* ☐ **Position it as working alongside the cane, not replacing it.** An eye-level camera cannot feel curbs, drop-offs or ground texture the way a cane does. Judges will ask about this.  
* ☐ **Pick the phone platform** for the glasses app (iOS or Android): whichever phone is paired with the glasses.  
* ☐ **Get glasses → phone → laptop frames working by midnight**, or switch to the webcam fallback.  
* ☐ **Agree the cut line:** P0 \= voice loop \+ describe/hazards \+ memory; P1 \= browser control; P2 \= work mode.  
* ☐ **Assign owners** for each workstream (Team roles section).

## **Scope**

Ship P0 end to end before anyone starts P1. Every mode is a spoken command routed to its own handler, so modes can be built in parallel and dropped independently.

| Priority | Mode | User says | What it does | Why it is in |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| P0 | Voice loop | anything | Speech from the glasses mic → intent router → spoken reply through the glasses speakers | Every mode needs it; it is the core of the Cartesia track |
| P0 | Describe & hazards (your \#1) | "What's in front of me?" · "What does the signal say?" | Continuous obstacle warnings; on request, reads the pedestrian signal and describes the scene | Most visceral demo and the clearest use of the glasses |
| P0 | Memory (your \#4) | "Where did I put my keys?" · "What was Sam wearing?" | Captions frames into a timeline, retrieves by meaning, answers with time and place | Biggest wow; carries the Moss, SpacetimeDB and Meta tracks |
| P1 | Laptop (your \#3) | "Email Sam that I'm running late" | Jev Ultrafast drives Chrome, reads the draft back and asks before sending | Mostly off-the-shelf; fast browser control is our edge |
| P2 | Work (your \#2) | "Is this the right item for order 12?" | Checks an item or label against a short task list, one step at a time | Shows what a cane cannot do, but is the hardest to demo convincingly |

Out of scope this weekend: turn-by-turn GPS navigation, recognizing strangers' faces, and any output that says a crossing is "safe".

## **Tech stack & architecture**

The phone app relays glasses frames and audio to one Python backend on a laptop, which routes each request to a mode and speaks the reply.

![system architecture · glasses to backend to modes and stores][image1]

system architecture · glasses to backend to modes and stores

Only the laptop calls cloud APIs. The phone just relays, so a webcam can stand in for the glasses without touching the backend.

| Layer | Pick | Sponsor track | Why this one |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Glasses I/O | Meta Wearables Device Access Toolkit | Meta | Official camera stream (up to 720p / 30 fps), mic and speakers |
| Phone relay | Swift (iOS) or Kotlin (Android) app |  | Required host for the toolkit; samples frames and forwards them |
| Backend | Python \+ FastAPI WebSockets on one laptop |  | Every SDK below has a Python client; plug into ethernet |
| Speech | Cartesia Ink 2 (in), Sonic 3.5 (out) | Cartesia | Streaming STT with turn detection; low-latency TTS |
| Intent routing | TypeSafe Jev |  | One typed decision per utterance, fast enough to feel instant |
| Vision | Ultralytics YOLO (local) \+ Claude Haiku 5.5 | Anthropic | Local detector for instant warnings; Claude for descriptions and signs |
| Reasoning | Claude Sonnet 5.5 | Anthropic | Recall answers, task checks, low-confidence intents |
| Browser control | Jev Ultrafast \+ Chrome |  | Open-source agent built on Jev; acts on the DOM, not screenshots |
| Memory store | SpacetimeDB (TypeScript module) | SpacetimeDB | Durable timeline plus live subscriptions for the dashboard |
| Memory search | Moss (Python SDK) | Moss | Sub-10 ms semantic \+ keyword search over captions |
| Family dashboard | React \+ SpacetimeDB TypeScript client | SpacetimeDB, Meta | Live alerts and recall thumbnails for a trusted person |

Claude model IDs: claude-haiku-5-5 and claude-sonnet-5-5.

## **Build notes per mode**

All modes share one pipe: glasses → phone app → laptop backend over a WebSocket. Build that pipe first; everything else plugs into it.

### **Shared: glasses → phone → laptop**

* **Phone app** uses the Meta Wearables Device Access Toolkit (iOS Swift Package, or Android via GitHub Packages, which needs a GitHub token). Flow: register the app (deeplinks to the Meta AI app), request camera permission, start a session.  
* **Video** streams over Bluetooth at up to 720p / 30 fps and drops automatically when bandwidth is tight. Sample \~5 fps, downscale to 480p JPEG, push to the laptop.  
* **Mic** comes in over Hands-Free Profile as 8 kHz mono (phone-call quality). **Speakers:** play TTS on the phone and it routes to the glasses.  
* **Start on MockDeviceKit tonight** so app work is not blocked on pairing. Fallback camera: a phone on a lanyard or one of our webcams, feeding the same WebSocket.

### **Voice loop \+ router**

* Cartesia Ink 2 streaming STT; its turn-end event triggers handling.  
* Jev classifies each utterance into describe \| signal \| recall \| remember \| browser \| task \| help. TypeSafe quotes 70–500 ms per decision. Low confidence → Claude Sonnet 5.5 handles it as open-ended.  
* Replies via Cartesia Sonic 3.5, streamed, two sentences max. Pre-generate fixed hazard phrases ("Stop, obstacle ahead") to cut latency.  
* Mirror the transcript and audio on the laptop screen: glasses speakers are open-ear, so judges will not hear them.

### **Describe & hazards (P0)**

* **Always-on:** a local object detector (Ultralytics YOLO, nano size) on the laptop at \~5 fps. Rule: a person, bike, car or furniture box that is large, centered and growing → short spoken warning with direction. 3-second cooldown per object so it does not nag.  
* **On request:** one frame → Claude Haiku 5.5 for scene descriptions and signal reading ("The walk sign is on. A car is turning from your left."). It never says a crossing is safe.  
* **Demo:** crosswalk footage on a monitor at our table, plus a chair in the walking path.

### **Memory (P0)**

* Every \~3 s or on scene change, Claude Haiku 5.5 captions the frame as JSON: objects and where they sit, named people and their clothing, the place, visible text.  
* Each moment becomes a SpacetimeDB row (time, caption, thumbnail); the caption text is indexed in Moss (built-in embeddings, hybrid keyword \+ semantic search).  
* **Recall:** Moss top-5 → Claude Sonnet 5.5 answers with time and place ("3:42 PM, kitchen counter, next to the fruit bowl") and pushes the thumbnail to the family dashboard.  
* **People:** only those the user names by voice ("this is my brother Sam") get labeled. No identification of strangers.  
* **"I'm lost":** sends the latest place note and Sam's description to the family dashboard.

### **Laptop control with Jev Ultrafast (P1)**

* browser-use/jev-ultrafast is MIT-licensed. It needs TYPESAFE\_API\_KEY and an OpenRouter-compatible TEXT\_MODEL\_API\_KEY, and attaches to Chrome through Browser Harness with remote debugging on.  
* Call it from Python as Agent(url, goal).run(). Operations: click, type text, select, scroll, wait, done, blocked.  
* **Known gaps:** frames, shadow roots, canvas, uploads and pop-up tabs are unsupported. Gmail compose may break, so test it tonight and pick a demo site that works.  
* Read every draft aloud and wait for "send" before any irreversible click. Use a throwaway demo account signed in to the Chrome profile; no credentials in code.

### **Work mode (P2)**

* One scripted task: a three-item "order" card. The user holds up each item; one Claude Sonnet 5.5 call compares the frame with the list and says the next step.  
* Only start this after Saturday's 6 PM feature freeze if P0 and P1 are solid.

## **Demo & judging plan**

Open with the user's problem in one line, then spend about 75 of our 120 seconds on a live demo that touches every P0 mode.

**Two-minute pitch:**

1. **0:00–0:15 · Who and why.** Name the community and quote one person we talked to this weekend.  
2. **0:15–1:30 · Live demo.** The wearer stays quiet; the glasses do the talking.  
   1. Walk toward the chair → "Stop, chair ahead, slightly left."  
   2. Face the crosswalk footage → "The walk sign is on. A car is turning from your left."  
   3. Keys were set down on camera earlier → "Where did I put my keys?" → time and place; the thumbnail appears on the dashboard.  
   4. "Email Sam that I'm at the Palace of Fine Arts" → draft read back → "Send."  
   5. "I'm lost" → family dashboard alert with Sam's description.  
3. **1:30–1:50 · How it is built.** One architecture slide naming Meta DAT, Cartesia, Jev, Claude, Moss and SpacetimeDB.  
4. **1:50–2:00 · Responsibility.** Works alongside the cane, never says "safe", stores only people the user names, one-tap delete.

**Table setup:**

* Laptop facing judges with the live transcript and family dashboard; laptop audio mirrors every spoken reply.  
* A monitor or tablet looping crosswalk footage, a chair and a set of keys.  
* Tables are shared by 2–3 teams, so use push-to-talk on the phone and switch to the phone mic if the room is loud.  
* A backup demo video, recorded Saturday night, ready to play if the wifi dies.

**Devpost checklist:**

* ☐ Draft submitted Saturday night; final by 8:30 AM Sunday (30-minute buffer)  
* ☐ All teammates added to the submission  
* ☐ Tracks selected: Meta, Anthropic, Cartesia, Moss, SpacetimeDB

## **Risks & open questions**

The biggest risk is the glasses stream, so it gets a hard midnight checkpoint with a webcam fallback. Everything else has a cheaper plan B.

| Risk | What breaks | Mitigation / fallback |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Glasses registration or firmware does not match the toolkit | No camera feed | Check the Version Dependencies page first; build on MockDeviceKit; switch to webcam or phone camera at midnight if still blocked |
| Bluetooth stream drops resolution under load | Blurry frames | Design for 480p; use single-frame photo capture for describe and recall requests |
| Venue wifi congested | Slow model calls | Ethernet adapter on the backend laptop; local detector; small JPEGs; optionally rent an ASUS Ascent GX10 (GB10, 128 GB unified memory) to run a vision model locally |
| 8 kHz glasses mic | Misheard commands | Short command phrases; phone mic fallback |
| One toolkit session at a time | Meta AI features unavailable while we stream | Do not depend on Meta AI; our app owns the session |
| Jev Ultrafast cannot handle the target site | Laptop demo fails | Test the exact site tonight; pick a simpler demo site; P1 is droppable |
| Overclaiming safety | Judges lose trust | "Alongside the cane" framing, no "safe" wording, a failure-modes slide |
| Recording bystanders | Code of Conduct and Meta acceptable-use issues | Store captions and small thumbnails only, label named people only, voice "delete" command, consent from anyone in the demo |
| Scope creep | Nothing works at 9 AM | Feature freeze Saturday 6 PM; P2 only after the freeze |

**Open questions:**

* ☐ Which glasses model and firmware do we have, and are they on the toolkit's supported list?  
* ☐ Whose TypeSafe key do we use, and does it have rate limits?  
* ☐ How many sponsor tracks can one Devpost submission enter?  
* ☐ Push-to-talk: phone button or voice activity? Tapping the glasses pauses the session, so it cannot be the trigger.  
* ☐ Who can we talk to this weekend who is blind or low-vision (mentors, Slack, friends) for the Anthropic quote?
